Title: Creation
DateApprox: Traditionally dated c. 4004 BC (chronology varies by tradition)
Events: God creates the heavens, earth, and humanity

Title: The Fall and Cain and Abel
Places: Garden of Eden; Land of Nod
Events: Humanity falls into sin; Cain murders Abel

Title: Enoch Walks with God
Events: Enoch walks faithfully with God and is taken up without dying

Title: Noah and the Flood
Events: God judges the earth with a flood; Noah builds the ark

Title: God's Covenant with Noah
Events: After the flood, God makes a covenant with Noah and his sons, promising never again to destroy all life with a flood, and gives the rainbow as the sign of that covenant.

Title: Noah's Blessing and the Curse of Canaan
KeyPersons: Noah; Shem; Ham; Japheth; Canaan, Son of Ham
Events: Noah becomes drunk and lies uncovered in his tent; Ham dishonours him, while Shem and Japheth cover him. When Noah awakes, he curses Canaan and blesses Shem and Japheth.

Title: Tower of Babel
Events: Languages are confused and peoples scatter

Title: Call of Abraham
Events: God calls Abram and promises land and descendants

Title: Abram in Egypt
Events: Fleeing famine, Abram goes down to Egypt, where Pharaoh takes Sarai into his house until plagues reveal the truth and Abram is sent away enriched.

Title: Abram, Lot, and Melchizedek
Events: Abram and Lot part ways; Abram rescues Lot and meets Melchizedek, priest of God Most High

Title: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
KeyPersons: Abraham; Sarah; Isaac; Rebekah; Jacob; Leah; Rachel
Events: Covenant promises pass to Isaac and Jacob; Jacob's 12 sons found Israel's tribes
ArchaeologicalFinds: Cave of Machpelah traditionally identified at Hebron

Title: Hagar and Ishmael
Events: Hagar bears Ishmael; God hears her in the wilderness and promises her son a future

Title: The Covenant of Circumcision
Events: God renames Abram as Abraham and Sarai as Sarah, establishes circumcision as the sign of the covenant, and promises a son through Sarah.

Title: Sodom and Gomorrah
Events: God judges Sodom and Gomorrah; Lot escapes the destruction

Title: Abraham and Abimelech
Events: God protects Sarah and Abraham in Gerar; Abraham prays for Abimelech

Title: Birth of Isaac
Events: Isaac, the child of promise, is born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age

Title: The Binding of Isaac
Events: God tests Abraham; he provides a ram in place of Isaac on the mountain

Title: Abraham Buys the Burial Cave
Events: After Sarah's death, Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah from Ephron the Hittite as a burial place, his first owned land in Canaan.

Title: Isaac and Rebekah
Events: Abraham's servant finds Rebekah; she marries Isaac and the promise continues

Title: Jacob and Esau: Birthright and Blessing
Events: Esau sells his birthright; Jacob receives Isaac's blessing and flees

Title: Isaac and Abimelech
Events: God renews the covenant with Isaac in Gerar; he prospers and makes peace with Abimelech

Title: Jacob's Ladder at Bethel
Events: Jacob dreams of a stairway to heaven; God renews the covenant with him at Bethel

Title: Jacob in Haran
Events: Jacob serves Laban, marries Leah and Rachel, and returns with his family and flocks

Title: Jacob Wrestles with God at Peniel
Events: Jacob wrestles through the night with God and is renamed Israel

Title: Dinah and Shechem
Events: After Dinah is violated by Shechem, her brothers Simeon and Levi take revenge on the city, and Jacob's family must flee the region.

Title: Jacob's Return and Reconciliation
Events: Jacob reconciles with Esau, returns to Bethel, and buries his father Isaac

Title: Jacob Returns to Bethel
Events: God tells Jacob to return to Bethel, where he builds an altar, God renews the covenant and the name Israel, and Rachel and Isaac die.

Title: God's Covenant with Abram
Events: God promises Abram descendants as numerous as the stars and the land of Canaan as their inheritance. Abram believes God, and the covenant is sealed with a ceremony in which a smoking furnace and a burning lamp pass between the divided animals.

Title: Hagar and Ishmael Sent Away
Events: After Isaac is weaned, Sarah asks Abraham to send Hagar and Ishmael away. God tells Abraham to listen to Sarah, promising to make a nation of Ishmael also, and God provides water for Hagar and Ishmael in the wilderness of Beersheba.

Title: Death of Abraham
Events: Abraham dies at a good old age, and his sons Isaac and Ishmael bury him in the cave of Machpelah, which he had bought from Ephron the Hittite.

Title: Death of Rachel and Birth of Benjamin
Events: On the journey from Bethel, Rachel dies giving birth to her second son. Jacob names the boy Benjamin, and Rachel is buried on the way to Bethlehem, where Jacob sets up a pillar on her grave.

Title: Death of Isaac
Events: Jacob comes to his father Isaac at Mamre, and Isaac dies at a good old age. His sons Esau and Jacob bury him.

Title: Joseph in Egypt
Events: Joseph is sold into Egypt, rises to power, and saves his family in famine

Title: Judah and Tamar
Events: Tamar secures her place in Judah's line; Perez is born, ancestor of David

Title: Job Endures Suffering
Events: Job remains faithful through suffering and is restored

Title: Jacob Blesses Ephraim and Manasseh
KeyPersons: Jacob; Joseph, Son of Jacob; Ephraim; Manasseh
Events: Near the end of his life in Egypt, Jacob adopts Joseph's sons Ephraim and Manasseh as his own and blesses them, deliberately crossing his hands so that the younger, Ephraim, receives the greater blessing.

Title: Death and Burial of Jacob
Events: Jacob dies in Egypt after charging his sons to bury him with his fathers. Joseph has him embalmed, and a great company escorts his body to Canaan, where he is buried in the cave of Machpelah.

Title: Death of Joseph
Events: Joseph dies in Egypt at the age of 110, after making his brothers swear to carry his bones up from Egypt when God visits them. He is embalmed and placed in a coffin in Egypt.

Title: Birth and Call of Moses - The Exodus Begins
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: Israel enslaved in Egypt; Moses is born, called at the burning bush, and leads the Exodus after the Passover

Title: The Ten Plagues
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: God sends ten plagues on Egypt; Pharaoh finally lets Israel go

Title: The Passover
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: On the night of the final plague, Israelite households mark their doorposts with lamb's blood and eat the Passover meal before leaving Egypt.

Title: Crossing the Red Sea
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: God parts the Red Sea; Israel crosses on dry ground and Pharaoh's army is drowned

Title: Manna and Quail
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: God provides manna and quail for Israel in the wilderness

Title: Water from the Rock and Victory over Amalek
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: God gives water from the rock at Rephidim; Israel defeats Amalek as Aaron and Hur hold up Moses' hands

Title: Jethro's Counsel
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: Jethro advises Moses to share the burden of judging Israel

Title: Law Given at Mount Sinai
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (approx., after Exodus)
Events: Ten Commandments given; Tabernacle built; sacrificial law established

Title: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
KeyPersons: Moses; Aaron; Nadab; Abihu; Eleazar; Ithamar
Events: Moses washes, clothes, and anoints Aaron and his sons, and fire from the Lord consumes the inaugural offering at the tabernacle.

Title: The Death of Nadab and Abihu
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: Nadab and Abihu offer unauthorized fire before the Lord and are consumed by fire, teaching Israel that worship must follow God's commands.

Title: The Blasphemer Stoned
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: A man who blasphemes the Name is brought before Moses, and the Lord commands that he be stoned, establishing the law of blasphemy.

Title: Israel Numbered at Sinai
Events: In the second year after the Exodus, God commands Moses to count the fighting men of Israel by tribe at Mount Sinai.

Title: The Levites Set Apart for Service
Events: The tribe of Levi is set apart in place of Israel's firstborn to carry, guard, and serve at the tabernacle.

Title: Fire at Taberah and the Quail
Events: The people complain, fire burns at the edge of the camp at Taberah, and when they crave meat God sends quail and a plague follows.

Title: Miriam and Aaron Oppose Moses
Events: Miriam and Aaron challenge Moses' authority, Miriam is struck with leprosy for seven days, and Moses intercedes for her healing.

Title: The Twelve Spies
Events: Twelve spies scout Canaan, ten report fearfully, Joshua and Caleb urge trust in God, and the people's rebellion brings forty years in the wilderness.

Title: The Covenant Sealed at Sinai
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: Israel seals the covenant at Sinai with sacrifices; the elders see God

Title: The Pattern of the Tabernacle
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: God shows Moses the pattern of the tabernacle and its furnishings on the mountain

Title: The Golden Calf
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: Israel worships a golden calf while Moses is on the mountain; the tablets are broken

Title: God's Glory and the Second Tablets
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: God renews the covenant; Moses returns with new tablets, his face shining with God's glory

Title: The Tabernacle Completed
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: The people build the tabernacle exactly as God showed Moses, Moses sets it up, and the glory of the Lord fills it.

Title: Wilderness Wanderings
Places: Sinai Wilderness; Kadesh Barnea; Plains of Moab
Events: Israel wanders 40 years; spies sent into Canaan; Moses reviews the law before his death

Title: Korah's Rebellion
KeyPersons: Moses; Aaron; Korah, Son of Izhar; Dathan; Abiram; Eleazar
Events: Korah, Dathan, and Abiram challenge the leadership of Moses and Aaron, and the earth swallows the rebels while fire consumes their followers.

Title: Aaron's Rod Buds
Events: To settle the rebellion's challenge, Aaron's staff alone buds, blossoms, and bears almonds, confirming God's choice of Aaron's priesthood.

Title: Moses Strikes the Rock at Meribah
Events: At Meribah, Moses strikes the rock instead of speaking to it as commanded, and God tells him he will not lead Israel into the land.

Title: The Deaths of Miriam and Aaron
Events: Miriam dies at Kadesh, and Aaron dies on Mount Hor, where his priestly garments are passed to his son Eleazar.

Title: The Bronze Serpent
Events: When fiery serpents bite the complaining people, God tells Moses to lift up a bronze serpent, and all who look at it live.

Title: Victory over Sihon and Og
Events: Israel defeats Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan, taking their lands east of the Jordan.

Title: Balaam Blesses Israel
Events: Hired by Balak to curse Israel, Balaam's donkey speaks, and God turns every attempted curse into a blessing over Israel.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Balaam Inscription (Deir Alla Inscription)

Title: Israel's Sin at Baal Peor
Events: Israel joins in worship of Baal of Peor and a plague breaks out until Phinehas acts and the plague stops.

Title: The Second Census
Events: On the plains of Moab, a new generation of Israel is counted before entering the promised land.

Title: The Daughters of Zelophehad
KeyPersons: Moses; Zelophehad; Mahlah; Noah, Daughter of Zelophehad; Hoglah; Milcah, Daughter of Zelophehad; Tirzah
Events: Zelophehad's five daughters ask for their father's inheritance, and God grants that daughters may inherit when there is no son.

Title: Joshua Succeeds Moses
Events: Before his death, Moses lays hands on Joshua, commissioning him to lead Israel into the promised land.

Title: The War Against Midian
Events: Israel wages war against Midian in judgment for Baal Peor, and the spoils are divided between the soldiers and the congregation.

Title: The Tribes Settle East of the Jordan
Events: Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh ask to settle east of the Jordan, promising to fight alongside their brothers until Canaan is conquered.

Title: The Hebrew Midwives Defy Pharaoh
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: Pharaoh orders the Hebrew midwives Shiphrah and Puah to kill newborn Hebrew sons, but the midwives fear God and let the children live. God deals well with the midwives, and Pharaoh then commands all Egypt to throw Hebrew sons into the river.

Title: Moses Flees to Midian
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: After killing an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew, Moses flees from Pharaoh to Midian, where he defends the daughters of Reuel at a well, is given Zipporah as his wife, and becomes a shepherd.

Title: The Burning Bush
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: While shepherding in Midian, Moses sees a bush burning without being consumed, and God calls to him from it, revealing himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and commissioning Moses to bring Israel out of Egypt. Moses objects that he is not able, and God gives him signs and promises Aaron's help.

Title: Moses Sets Out for Egypt
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: Moses returns to Jethro, takes his wife and sons, and sets out for Egypt with the rod of God. On the way, the LORD seeks to kill Moses, and Zipporah circumcises their son, after which the LORD lets him go.

Title: Moses and Aaron Before the Elders
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: Aaron meets Moses at the mountain of God, and together they gather the elders of Israel, speak all the words God has given Moses, and perform the signs. The people believe, and bow their heads and worship.

Title: The Pillar of Cloud and Fire
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: As Israel leaves Egypt, the LORD goes before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night, guiding their journey and never departing from before the people.

Title: The Passover at Sinai
Events: In the second year after the exodus, Israel keeps the Passover in the wilderness of Sinai as commanded. Men made unclean by a dead body ask how they may keep it, and God provides a second Passover a month later for those unclean or on a journey.

Title: Israel Departs from Sinai
Places: Wilderness of Sinai; Wilderness of Paran
Events: On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud lifts from the tabernacle and Israel sets out from Sinai in marching order behind the ark. Moses urges Hobab to stay and be as eyes for them in the wilderness.

Title: The Sabbath-Breaker Stoned
Events: While Israel is in the wilderness, a man is found gathering sticks on the Sabbath day and is brought before Moses and Aaron. The LORD commands that the man be stoned, and the whole congregation stones him outside the camp.

Title: Edom Refuses Israel Passage
Events: From Kadesh, Moses asks the king of Edom for passage along the king's highway, promising to pay for any water drunk. Edom refuses and comes out against Israel with a strong force, so Israel turns away from him.

Title: Victory at Hormah
Events: The king of Arad attacks Israel and takes some prisoners, and Israel vows to utterly destroy the Canaanite cities if the LORD delivers them. The LORD listens, Israel defeats the Canaanites, and the place is called Hormah.

Title: The Covenant Renewed in Moab
Events: On the plains of Moab, Moses renews the covenant with the new generation, setting before them life and death, blessing and curse.

Title: The Death of Moses
Events: Moses views the promised land from Mount Nebo, dies there, and is buried by the Lord while Joshua takes up leadership.

Title: Conquest of Canaan
Events: Joshua leads Israel into Canaan; Jericho falls; land is divided among tribes
ArchaeologicalFinds: Merneptah Stele (c. 1208 BC) - earliest extra-biblical mention of Israel

Title: Rahab Hides the Spies
DateApprox: c. 1406 BC or c. 1230 BC (date debated)
Events: Two Israelite spies are hidden by Rahab in Jericho, and she is spared when the city falls for protecting them.

Title: Crossing the Jordan
DateApprox: c. 1406 BC or c. 1230 BC (date debated)
Events: Israel crosses the Jordan River on dry ground as the priests carry the ark, and stones of remembrance are set up at Gilgal.

Title: The Walls of Jericho
DateApprox: c. 1406 BC or c. 1230 BC (date debated)
Events: After marching around Jericho for seven days, Israel shouts and the city walls fall, giving Israel its first victory in Canaan.

Title: Defeat and Capture of Ai
DateApprox: c. 1406 BC or c. 1230 BC (date debated)
Events: After an initial defeat caused by Achan's sin, Israel repents and captures Ai by ambush, pressing the conquest inland.

Title: The Commander of the Lord's Army Appears to Joshua
DateApprox: c. 1406 BC or c. 1230 BC (date debated)
Events: Before attacking Jericho, Joshua meets the commander of the Lord's army, who tells him to remove his sandals because the ground is holy.

Title: Covenant Renewed at Mount Ebal
DateApprox: c. 1406 BC or c. 1230 BC (date debated)
Events: After the capture of Ai, Joshua builds an altar on Mount Ebal, writes the law on stones, and reads the blessings and curses before all Israel.

Title: The Southern Campaign and the Sun Stands Still
DateApprox: c. 1406 BC or c. 1230 BC (date debated)
Places: Gibeon; Aijalon; Makkedah; Libnah; Lachish; Eglon; Debir; Jarmuth
Events: After the Gibeonites make a treaty with Israel, Joshua defends Gibeon against five Amorite kings, and the sun stands still over Gibeon and the moon over the Valley of Aijalon while Israel completes the victory.

Title: The Northern Campaign and the Fall of Hazor
DateApprox: c. 1406 BC or c. 1230 BC (date debated)
Events: A northern coalition led by Jabin of Hazor gathers at the Waters of Merom, but Joshua defeats it by surprise and burns Hazor, breaking the last organised Canaanite resistance.

Title: Joshua's Farewell and Covenant Renewal
DateApprox: c. 1375 BC or c. 1200 BC (date debated)
Events: At the end of his life Joshua gathers Israel at Shechem, recounts God's faithfulness, and calls the people to choose whom they will serve.

Title: Period of the Judges
KeyPersons: Deborah; Gideon; Samson; Jephthah; Ehud; Barak
Events: Cycle of sin, oppression, repentance, and deliverance by judges

Title: Othniel Delivers Israel
DateApprox: c. 1350 BC (approx., during the period of the Judges)
Events: When Israel is oppressed by Cushan-rishathaim of Aram, the Spirit of the Lord comes on Othniel, who defeats the oppressor and brings the land forty years of rest.

Title: Ehud Delivers Israel from Moab
DateApprox: c. 1300 BC (approx., during the period of the Judges)
Events: The left-handed judge Ehud kills the Moabite king Eglon and leads Israel to victory, bringing eighty years of peace.

Title: Deborah and Barak Defeat Sisera
DateApprox: c. 1200 BC (approx., during the period of the Judges)
KeyPersons: Deborah; Barak; Jael; Jabin, King of Hazor
Events: Under Deborah's direction Barak defeats the Canaanite general Sisera at the Kishon, and Jael kills the fleeing Sisera.

Title: Gideon's Victory over Midian
DateApprox: c. 1150 BC (approx., during the period of the Judges)
Events: With only three hundred men, Gideon routs the Midianite army by night with trumpets, jars, and torches, showing the victory belongs to God.

Title: Abimelech's Coup at Shechem
DateApprox: c. 1150 BC (approx., during the period of the Judges)
KeyPersons: Abimelech, Son of Gideon; Jotham, Son of Gideon
Events: Gideon's son Abimelech murders his seventy brothers and is made king at Shechem, until Jotham's parable of judgment is fulfilled in civil war and Abimelech's death.

Title: The Danites Capture Laish
DateApprox: c. 1150 BC (approx., during the period of the Judges)
Events: Unable to hold their allotted territory, the tribe of Dan migrates north, captures the peaceful city of Laish, and renames it Dan, setting up Micah's idol there.

Title: Jephthah and His Vow
DateApprox: c. 1100 BC (approx., during the period of the Judges)
Events: Jephthah defeats the Ammonites but is bound by a rash vow he made before the battle, a warning about careless promises to God.

Title: Samson and Delilah
DateApprox: c. 1100-1050 BC (approx., during the period of the Judges)
Events: Samson, judge of Israel, is betrayed by Delilah, loses his strength when his hair is cut, and in his death pulls down the Philistine temple.

Title: Ruth and Boaz
Events: Ruth's loyalty leads to redemption and a place in David's lineage

Title: Samuel - Last Judge and Prophet
Events: Samuel anoints Israel's first kings

Title: Calling of Samuel
Events: As a boy serving at Shiloh, Samuel hears God's voice in the night and is established as a prophet to all Israel.

Title: Capture and Return of the Ark
Events: The Philistines capture the ark of God in battle, but after plagues fall on their cities they return it to Israel.

Title: The Levite's Concubine and War with Benjamin
DateApprox: c. 1100 BC (approx., during the period of the Judges)
Events: After a Levite's concubine is murdered at Gibeah, the outraged tribes go to war against Benjamin, nearly wiping out the tribe before arranging wives for its survivors.

Title: Samuel's Victory at Mizpah
Events: After the ark's return, Samuel calls Israel to repentance at Mizpah, and when the Philistines attack, the Lord thunders against them and Israel routs them, setting up the Ebenezer stone.

Title: Anointing of Saul as King
Events: Samuel anoints Saul as Israel's first king, and Saul is publicly confirmed as king at Mizpah.

Title: Saul - First King of Israel
Events: Saul is anointed king, later rejected for disobedience

Title: Saul's Victory at Jabesh-gilead
Events: When the Ammonites threaten Jabesh-gilead, Saul rallies Israel, relieves the city at dawn, and is confirmed as king by the people.

Title: Saul Rejected as King
Events: Saul offers the sacrifice himself at Gilgal instead of waiting for Samuel, and later spares Amalekite spoil against God's command; Samuel announces that the Lord has rejected him as king.

Title: Jonathan's Victory at Michmash
KeyPersons: Jonathan, Son of Saul; King Saul
Events: Jonathan and his armour-bearer climb to the Philistine garrison at Michmash and rout it, throwing the whole Philistine camp into panic.

Title: David Anointed by Samuel
Events: Samuel is sent to Bethlehem, where God chooses David, the youngest son of Jesse, and anoints him as Israel's future king.

Title: David and Goliath
Events: The young shepherd David defeats the Philistine champion Goliath with a sling and stone, trusting in God rather than armour.

Title: David and Jonathan
Events: Jonathan, Saul's son, befriends David and protects him from his father's jealousy, making a covenant of loyal friendship.

Title: David Spares Saul
Events: Though he has the chance to kill Saul twice, David twice refuses to strike down the Lord's anointed and leaves vengeance to God.

Title: Massacre of the Priests at Nob
Events: Fleeing Saul, David receives bread and Goliath's sword at Nob; when Doeg reports it, Saul orders the priests of Nob killed, and Doeg slaughters eighty-five of them.

Title: Death of Samuel
Events: Samuel dies and all Israel gathers to mourn and bury him at Ramah, closing the ministry of the last judge before Saul's final years.

Title: Death of Saul at Mount Gilboa
Events: Saul and his son Jonathan fall in battle against the Philistines at Mount Gilboa, ending Saul's reign and opening the way for David.

Title: David - King and Psalmist
Events: David unites Israel, captures Jerusalem, receives the Davidic covenant; many Psalms attributed to David
ArchaeologicalFinds: Tel Dan Stele mentions House of David; Mesha Stele also references Davidic lineage (interpretation debated)

Title: David Becomes King
Events: David is first made king over Judah at Hebron, then over all Israel, and captures Jerusalem as his capital.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Tel Dan Stele (House of David)

Title: Saul Consults the Medium at Endor
Events: With Samuel dead and God silent, Saul disguises himself and consults a medium at Endor, who brings up Samuel; Samuel foretells Saul's defeat and death the next day.

Title: David at Ziklag and the Amalekite Raid
Events: While David is away, Amalekites raid Ziklag and carry off its people; David pursues them, recovers everyone and everything, and shares the spoil equally with those who stayed behind.

Title: War with the House of Saul
KeyPersons: King David; Joab; Abner, Son of Ner; Ish-bosheth, Son of Saul
Events: After Saul's death David rules Judah from Hebron while Ish-bosheth rules the north, and a long civil war follows until Abner and then Ish-bosheth are murdered and all Israel turns to David.

Title: Ark Brought to Jerusalem
Events: David brings the ark of God up to Jerusalem with singing and dancing, establishing the city as Israel's worship centre.

Title: Davidic Covenant
Events: Through Nathan, God promises David an enduring house and a throne established forever, pointing forward to the Messiah.

Title: David's Kindness to Mephibosheth
KeyPersons: King David; Mephibosheth, Son of Jonathan; Jonathan, Son of Saul
Events: For Jonathan's sake David seeks out Jonathan's lame son Mephibosheth, restores Saul's lands to him, and seats him permanently at the king's table.

Title: David's Conquests
Events: David defeats the Philistines, Moab, the Arameans of Damascus and Edom, garrisons the conquered lands, and makes Israel the dominant power of the region.

Title: David and Bathsheba
Events: David commits adultery with Bathsheba and arranges Uriah's death, then repents when confronted by Nathan the prophet.

Title: David's War with Ammon
Events: After the Ammonites humiliate David's envoys, Israel fights a long war against Ammon and its Aramean allies, ending with Joab's capture of Rabbah, the Ammonite capital.

Title: Amnon, Tamar, and Absalom's Revenge
KeyPersons: Amnon, Son of David; Absalom; King David
Events: David's son Amnon assaults his half-sister Tamar; two years later her brother Absalom murders Amnon at a feast and flees, fracturing David's household.

Title: Absalom's Rebellion
Events: David's son Absalom rebels and seizes Jerusalem, but his revolt is defeated in the forest of Ephraim and he is killed.

Title: Sheba's Rebellion
KeyPersons: King David; Joab; Sheba, Son of Bichri; Amasa, Son of Ithra
Events: As David returns from Absalom's rebellion, Sheba son of Bichri raises a fresh northern revolt; Joab pursues him to Abel-beth-maachah, where the city surrenders Sheba's head to end the siege.

Title: Famine and the Gibeonites
KeyPersons: King David; Mephibosheth, Son of Saul
Events: A three-year famine is traced to Saul's broken treaty with the Gibeonites; David hands over seven of Saul's descendants, the famine ends, and Saul's family is finally buried with honour.

Title: David's Census and the Plague
Events: David's census of Israel brings a plague on the land, stopped at the threshing floor of Araunah, where David builds an altar.

Title: Solomon and the First Temple
KeyPersons: Solomon; Queen of Sheba; Hiram of Tyre
BibleBooks: 1 Kings; 2 Chronicles; Proverbs; Ecclesiastes; Song of Solomon
Events: Solomon builds the First Temple; famed for wisdom literature

Title: Solomon Succeeds David
KeyPersons: King Solomon; King David; Adonijah; Zadok, High Priest; Benaiah, Son of Jehoiada; Nathan
Events: As David lies dying, Adonijah claims the throne, but David has Solomon anointed instead; Solomon secures the kingdom, and David charges him to keep God's law.

Title: Solomon's Dream at Gibeon and Wise Judgment
Events: At Gibeon God appears to Solomon in a dream and grants his request for wisdom; Solomon's judgment between two women claiming one baby soon displays that wisdom to all Israel.

Title: Building of Solomon's Temple
Events: Solomon builds the first temple in Jerusalem over seven years, and God's glory fills it at its dedication.

Title: Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon
Events: The Queen of Sheba visits Solomon to test him with hard questions and is overwhelmed by his wisdom and the splendour of his court.

Title: Song of Solomon Written
DateApprox: Traditionally Solomon c. 970-931 BC (date debated; some scholars place it later)
Events: A collection of love poems traditionally attributed to Solomon, celebrating love and marriage, is written and preserved as the Song of Solomon.

Title: Solomon's Apostasy and Adversaries
Events: In his later years Solomon's foreign wives turn his heart to other gods, and God raises adversaries against him, announcing that the kingdom will be torn from his son.

Title: Kingdom Divides - Israel and Judah
Events: Kingdom splits into northern Israel and southern Judah after Solomon's death

Title: Jeroboam's Golden Calves
Events: To stop his people returning to Jerusalem, Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan, appoints non-Levitical priests, and invents a rival feast, fixing Israel's idolatry for generations.

Title: The Man of God and Jeroboam's Altar
Events: A man of God from Judah cries against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel; the altar splits, Jeroboam's hand withers and is restored, and the prophet is killed by a lion for disobeying God's word on the way home.

Title: Shishak Invades Judah
Events: In Rehoboam's fifth year Shishak of Egypt invades Judah and plunders the treasures of the temple and palace, after which Rehoboam replaces the gold shields with bronze ones.

Title: Abijah Defeats Jeroboam
Events: Abijah of Judah appeals to the covenant with David before battle, and though Jeroboam ambushes him from behind, Judah routs the larger northern army and captures its border towns.

Title: Asa's Reforms and Wars
Events: Asa removes idols and deposes the queen mother for idolatry, defeats a vast Cushite army, and later wars with Baasha of Israel, who fortifies Ramah against Judah.

Title: Baasha's Coup
Events: Baasha assassinates Nadab at Gibbethon, wipes out the whole house of Jeroboam as prophesied, and reigns from Tirzah while continuing Jeroboam's sins.

Title: Zimri's Coup and Omri's Rise
KeyPersons: Zimri, King of Israel; Omri, King of Israel
Events: Zimri murders Elah and reigns only seven days before Omri, proclaimed king by the army, besieges Tirzah; Zimri burns the palace over himself, and Omri founds Samaria as Israel's new capital.

Title: Ahab's Wars with Syria and Death at Ramoth-gilead
KeyPersons: King Ahab; Ben-hadad, King of Syria; King Jehoshaphat
Events: Ahab twice defeats Ben-hadad of Syria, then joins Jehoshaphat to retake Ramoth-gilead, where a random arrow kills Ahab in disguise, fulfilling the word against him.

Title: Naboth's Vineyard
Events: King Ahab and Jezebel have Naboth falsely accused and stoned so they can seize his vineyard, and Elijah pronounces God's judgment on them.

Title: Jehoshaphat's Victory by Praise
Events: Facing invasion, King Jehoshaphat sets singers ahead of his army, and the Lord turns the invading armies against one another.

Title: Elijah and Elisha
KeyPersons: Elijah; Elisha; King Ahab; Jezebel; Jehu
Events: Prophets confront Baal worship; Elijah taken to heaven; Elisha succeeds him

Title: Elijah on Mount Carmel
Events: On Mount Carmel, fire from heaven consumes Elijah's sacrifice while Baal's prophets fail, turning the people back to the Lord.

Title: Elijah at Mount Horeb
Events: Fleeing Jezebel, Elijah meets God at Horeb not in wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a still small voice, and is sent back to his work.

Title: Elijah Taken Up; Elisha Succeeds Him
Events: Elijah is taken up to heaven in a whirlwind, and Elisha receives a double portion of his spirit and takes up his mantle.

Title: Naaman Healed of Leprosy
Events: Naaman, commander of Syria's army, is healed of leprosy after washing seven times in the Jordan at Elisha's word.

Title: Jehoram of Judah and Edom's Revolt
Events: Jehoram murders his brothers to secure the throne, marries into Ahab's house, and walks in Israel's ways; Edom and Libnah revolt against Judah and are never recovered.

Title: Jehu's Revolt
Events: Jehu is anointed king and wipes out the house of Ahab, including Jezebel, ending Baal worship's royal backing in Israel.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III

Title: Joash Preserved and Crowned
Events: The infant prince Joash, sole surviving heir of David's line, is hidden in the temple from Queen Athaliah and crowned king at age seven.

Title: Jeroboam II Restores Israel's Borders
Events: Under Jeroboam II Israel recovers the territory from Lebo-hamath to the Dead Sea and retakes Damascus, a final period of northern strength before the Assyrian advance.

Title: Jonah and Nineveh
DateApprox: c. 790-750 BC (traditional, under Jeroboam II; date debated)
Events: Jonah, sent to the Assyrian capital Nineveh, preaches repentance and the whole city turns from its evil, showing God's mercy reaching beyond Israel.

Title: Amaziah's Defeat by Jehoash
Events: Amaziah, fresh from defeating Edom, challenges Jehoash of Israel; Israel routs Judah at Beth-shemesh, breaks down Jerusalem's wall, and plunders the temple and palace.

Title: Amos's Ministry
Events: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, preaches justice and righteousness at Bethel, denouncing Israel's oppression of the poor and warning of coming judgment.

Title: Early Writing Prophets - Amos, Hosea, Jonah, Obadiah, Joel
Events: Prophets call Israel and Judah to justice, repentance, and covenant faithfulness

Title: Amos Confronted at Bethel
KeyPersons: Amos; Amaziah; Jeroboam II, King of Israel
Events: Amaziah, priest of Bethel, accuses Amos of conspiracy and orders him out of Israel, but Amos answers that God took him from following the flock and pronounces judgment on Amaziah's house.

Title: Hosea's Ministry
Events: Hosea's marriage to Gomer and his preaching picture Israel's unfaithfulness and God's pursuing love, calling the northern kingdom back before its fall.

Title: Joel's Ministry
Events: Joel calls Judah to repentance after a devastating locust plague, proclaiming the day of the Lord and the promise of God's Spirit poured out on all people.

Title: Hosea's Sign-Children
Events: Hosea's children are given names that are themselves messages: Jezreel warns of bloodshed repaid, Lo-Ruhamah declares mercy withdrawn, and Lo-Ammi declares 'not my people,' making his family a living sign of Israel's broken covenant.

Title: Menahem Pays Tribute to Assyria
KeyPersons: Menahem, King of Israel; Pul, King of Assyria
Events: After seizing the throne by violence, Menahem exacts silver from Israel's wealthy men to pay Pul of Assyria, buying Assyria's withdrawal and confirming its grip on Israel.

Title: Uzziah Struck with Leprosy
Events: Uzziah, strong after decades of success, enters the temple to burn incense himself; the priests resist him, leprosy breaks out on his forehead, and he lives apart until his death.

Title: Isaiah and Micah in Judah
Events: Isaiah prophesies judgment and messianic hope; Micah calls for justice
ArchaeologicalFinds: Hezekiah's Tunnel and Siloam Inscription in Jerusalem

Title: Isaiah's Call
Events: In the temple Isaiah sees the Lord high and lifted up, is cleansed by a burning coal, and answers God's call with, 'Here am I; send me.'

Title: Micah's Ministry
Events: Micah preaches in Judah under Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, condemning corrupt leaders and promising a ruler from Bethlehem who will shepherd God's people.

Title: The Syro-Ephraimite War
KeyPersons: Pekah, King of Israel; Ahaz, King of Judah; Tiglath-Pileser, King of Assyria
Events: Pekah of Israel and Rezin of Syria besiege Jerusalem to replace Ahaz; Ahaz appeals to Tiglath-Pileser of Assyria, who destroys Damascus, carries Israel's north into exile, and leaves Judah a vassal.

Title: Isaiah's Signs to Ahaz
DateApprox: c. 735-732 BC (approx., during the Syro-Ephraimite crisis)
KeyPersons: Isaiah; Ahaz, King of Judah; Shear-jashub; Maher-shalal-hash-baz
Events: As Syria and Israel threaten Jerusalem, Isaiah meets Ahaz with his son Shear-jashub ('a remnant shall return'), offers a sign Ahaz refuses, and announces the Immanuel sign; Isaiah then writes on a tablet and names a second son Maher-shalal-hash-baz ('speed to the spoil'), a sign that Assyria will strip Damascus and Samaria.

Title: Fall of Northern Israel to Assyria
Events: Assyria conquers Samaria; northern tribes exiled
ArchaeologicalFinds: Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III depicts Jehu; Assyrian annals record Samaria's fall

Title: Proverbs Collected
DateApprox: Proverbs of Solomon c. 970-931 BC; copied by the men of Hezekiah c. 715-686 BC; later sayings added (compilation date debated)
Events: Solomon's proverbs are gathered together with the sayings of Agur and Lemuel, including proverbs copied by the men of Hezekiah, forming the book of Proverbs.

Title: Hezekiah, Josiah, and Judah's Reforms
KeyPersons: Hezekiah; King Josiah; Jeremiah; Zephaniah; Nahum; Habakkuk
BibleBooks: 2 Kings; 2 Chronicles; Jeremiah; Zephaniah; Nahum; Habakkuk
Events: Hezekiah resists Assyria; Josiah rediscovers the Book of the Law and reforms Judah; prophets warn of Babylon
ArchaeologicalFinds: Sennacherib Prism records campaign against Hezekiah; Lachish Reliefs; Ketef Hinnom scrolls (c. 7th-6th c. BC) preserve priestly blessing

Title: Isaiah's Barefoot Sign
DateApprox: c. 711 BC (the year Tartan took Ashdod)
Events: In the year Assyria's commander captures Ashdod, Isaiah walks naked and barefoot for three years as a sign that Assyria will lead Egypt and Ethiopia away captive, warning Judah not to trust them for deliverance.

Title: Hezekiah and Sennacherib's Invasion
Events: When Sennacherib of Assyria besieges Jerusalem, Hezekiah prays and the angel of the Lord strikes the Assyrian camp, lifting the siege.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Sennacherib Prism (Taylor Prism); Hezekiah's Tunnel and Siloam Inscription; Lachish Reliefs

Title: Hezekiah's Tunnel
Events: Preparing for Sennacherib's invasion, Hezekiah cuts a tunnel through solid rock to bring the Gihon spring's water inside Jerusalem's walls, a feat still visible today.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Siloam Inscription, found in Hezekiah's Tunnel, describing the tunnelers meeting underground

Title: Hezekiah's Illness and Recovery
Events: Told he will die, Hezekiah prays and weeps; Isaiah returns with God's promise of fifteen more years, and the shadow on the sundial moves backward as a sign.

Title: Hezekiah Shows His Treasures to Babylon
DateApprox: During King Hezekiah's reign, after his recovery (date debated)
Events: Envoys from Merodach-baladan of Babylon visit Hezekiah, who shows them all his treasures and armoury, and Isaiah announces that everything in the palace will one day be carried to Babylon.

Title: Manasseh's Captivity and Repentance
Events: Manasseh, Judah's most idolatrous king, is captured by Assyrian commanders and taken to Babylon in chains; there he humbles himself, prays, and on returning to Jerusalem removes the idols he had set up.

Title: Jeremiah's Linen Girdle
Events: Jeremiah wears a linen girdle, buries it by the Euphrates at God's command, and digs it up ruined, a sign that Judah's pride will likewise rot in exile.

Title: Jeremiah's Broken Flask at Tophet
Events: Before the elders and priests in the Valley of Hinnom, Jeremiah breaks a potter's flask and declares that Jerusalem will be broken beyond mending for its idolatry at Tophet.

Title: Jeremiah Imprisoned by Pashhur
Events: Pashhur, chief governor of the temple, hears Jeremiah's prophecy, beats him, and puts him in the stocks at the upper gate of Benjamin until the next day, when Jeremiah renames him Magor-missabib, 'terror on every side.'

Title: Josiah's Reforms and the Book of the Law
Events: The rediscovered Book of the Law in the temple sparks Josiah's sweeping reforms, renewing the covenant and cleansing Judah's worship.

Title: Nahum's Prophecy Against Nineveh
DateApprox: c. 660-630 BC (before Nineveh's fall in 612 BC)
Events: Nahum prophesies the fall of Nineveh, the Assyrian capital that had destroyed the northern kingdom, declaring that God will judge violent empires.

Title: Zephaniah's Ministry
Events: Zephaniah warns Judah of the coming day of the Lord against idolatry and injustice, and promises a humble remnant that will trust in the Lord.

Title: Jeremiah's Call
Events: Jeremiah is called as a prophet while still young, appointed to uproot and plant, and sent to warn Judah even though his message will be rejected.

Title: Habakkuk's Dialogue with God
Events: Habakkuk questions God about injustice in Judah and the rise of Babylon, and learns that the righteous shall live by faith.

Title: Death of Josiah and Deposition of Jehoahaz
KeyPersons: King Josiah; Jehoahaz, King of Judah; Pharaoh Necho
Events: Josiah marches out against Pharaoh Necho at Megiddo and is killed; his son Jehoahaz reigns three months before Necho deposes him, fines Judah, and installs Jehoiakim.

Title: Jeremiah's Temple Sermon and Trial
DateApprox: c. 608 BC (approx., at the beginning of Jehoiakim's reign)
Events: Jeremiah preaches in the temple court that Jerusalem will fall like Shiloh unless Judah repents; priests and prophets seize him and demand death, but the princes acquit him, citing Micah's preaching under Hezekiah, which went unpunished.

Title: Jehoiakim Burns Jeremiah's Scroll
DateApprox: c. 605-604 BC (fourth and fifth years of Jehoiakim)
KeyPersons: Jeremiah; Baruch; Jehoiakim, King of Judah; Gemariah, Son of Shaphan
Events: Baruch writes Jeremiah's words on a scroll and reads them in the temple; after the princes warn the king, Jehoiakim cuts the scroll with a penknife and burns it leaf by leaf in the winter fire, and Jeremiah dictates the scroll again with many more words added.

Title: Jeremiah's Letter to the Exiles
KeyPersons: Jeremiah; Elasah; Zedekiah, King of Judah
Events: From Jerusalem, Jeremiah sends a letter by Elasah to the exiles already carried to Babylon, telling them to build, plant, and seek the city's peace, for their exile will last seventy years before God brings them back.

Title: Jeremiah's Yoke and Hananiah
KeyPersons: Jeremiah; Hananiah, the False Prophet; Zedekiah, King of Judah
Events: Jeremiah wears a wooden yoke as a sign that Judah must submit to Babylon, and when the prophet Hananiah breaks the yoke and promises freedom within two years, Jeremiah replaces it with a yoke of iron and announces Hananiah's death within the year.

Title: Jeremiah and the Fall of Jerusalem
Events: Babylon conquers Judah; First Temple destroyed; Jeremiah laments Jerusalem
ArchaeologicalFinds: Babylonian Chronicles; Lachish Letters

Title: Daniel Taken to Babylon
Events: Daniel and his friends are taken to Babylon, where Daniel resolves not to defile himself with the king's food and God gives him understanding in visions and dreams.

Title: Daniel Interprets the King's Dream
Events: Daniel tells and interprets Nebuchadnezzar's dream of a great statue, revealing that God sets up and removes kings and will establish an everlasting kingdom.

Title: Jehoiachin's Surrender and the Second Deportation
KeyPersons: Jehoiachin, King of Judah; King Nebuchadnezzar
Events: After a three-month reign, Jehoiachin surrenders to Nebuchadnezzar, who carries him, his court, and Jerusalem's craftsmen and treasures to Babylon in the second deportation.

Title: Ezekiel's Call
Events: By the River Chebar in Babylon, Ezekiel sees the glory of the Lord and is called as a watchman to speak God's word to the exiles.

Title: Ezekiel's Sign-Acts of the Siege
Events: Ezekiel acts out the siege of Jerusalem with a clay brick, lying on his side, and shaved hair, warning the exiles that Jerusalem will indeed fall.

Title: Ezekiel's Vision of the Temple Abominations
Events: In vision Ezekiel is carried from the exiles by the Chebar to the Jerusalem temple, where he is shown its secret idolatries, and watches the glory of the Lord depart from the temple and the city to the mountain east of the city.

Title: Death of Ezekiel's Wife
DateApprox: c. 588 BC (at the start of the siege of Jerusalem)
Events: At the opening of the siege of Jerusalem, Ezekiel's wife dies, and God forbids him to mourn aloud, making his restrained grief a sign that the exiles will likewise lose temple and loved ones without open mourning.

Title: Jeremiah in the Cistern
DateApprox: c. 588-586 BC (during the Babylonian siege of Jerusalem)
KeyPersons: Jeremiah; Ebed-Melech; Zedekiah, King of Judah
Events: During the siege, Jeremiah is arrested as a deserter, beaten, and lowered into a miry cistern to die, until Ebed-Melech pleads with Zedekiah and lifts him out with old rags and ropes.

Title: Jeremiah Buys a Field During the Siege
DateApprox: 587 BC (during the Babylonian siege of Jerusalem)
Events: While Jerusalem is under siege, Jeremiah buys a field at Anathoth as a sign that God will one day restore his people to the land.

Title: Obadiah's Ministry
Events: Obadiah pronounces judgment on Edom for standing by and rejoicing when Jerusalem fell, and promises that deliverance will come from Mount Zion.

Title: Ezekiel and Daniel in Exile
KeyPersons: Ezekiel; Daniel; Hananiah; Mishael; Azariah; Nebuchadnezzar; Belshazzar
Events: Ezekiel prophesies to exiles; Daniel remains faithful in Babylonian and Persian courts

Title: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the Fiery Furnace
Events: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refuse to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image and are thrown into a fiery furnace, where God preserves them unharmed.

Title: Nebuchadnezzar's Madness and Restoration
DateApprox: During the reign of King Nebuchadnezzar (date debated)
Events: After Daniel warns him from a dream of a great tree cut down, Nebuchadnezzar boasts of Babylon and loses his reason, living like a beast until he lifts his eyes to heaven, when his understanding and kingdom are restored and he blesses the Most High.

Title: Ezekiel's Vision of the Valley of Dry Bones
DateApprox: During Ezekiel's ministry, c. 593-571 BC (vision undated)
Events: Ezekiel sees a valley of dry bones come to life, a vision that God will restore his scattered people and put his Spirit within them.

Title: Jeremiah Freed After Jerusalem's Fall
Events: After Babylon takes Jerusalem, Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, releases Jeremiah from his chains at Ramah and lets him choose his way, and Jeremiah chooses to remain with Gedaliah and the remnant at Mizpah.

Title: Murder of Gedaliah
KeyPersons: Gedaliah, Son of Ahikam; Ishmael, Son of Nethaniah; Johanan, Son of Kareah
Events: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, though warned against, murders Gedaliah, Babylon's governor of the remnant, at Mizpah and massacres his men, and Johanan son of Kareah recovers the captives from him at Gibeon.

Title: Jeremiah Taken to Egypt
KeyPersons: Jeremiah; Johanan, Son of Kareah; Baruch
Events: Against Jeremiah's word that they must stay, Johanan and the remnant carry Jeremiah and Baruch down to Egypt, reaching Tahpanhes, where Jeremiah buries stones at Pharaoh's house as a sign that Babylon will conquer Egypt too.

Title: News of Jerusalem's Fall Reaches Ezekiel
Events: A fugitive from Jerusalem reaches the exiles and tells Ezekiel the city has fallen, and that evening Ezekiel's mouth, long shut as a sign, is opened and he is no longer mute.

Title: Ezekiel's Vision of the New Temple
Events: Ezekiel is shown a new temple and a river of life flowing from it, picturing God's restored presence among his people.

Title: Jehoiachin Released from Prison
KeyPersons: Jehoiachin, King of Judah; Evil-Merodach, King of Babylon
Events: In the first year of Evil-merodach, thirty-seven years after his deportation, Jehoiachin is released from prison, given a seat above the other captive kings, and fed at the king's table for life.

Title: Daniel's Visions of Kingdoms
DateApprox: c. 553-536 BC (first year of Belshazzar to third year of Cyrus)
Events: Across the reigns of Belshazzar, Darius, and Cyrus, Daniel receives a series of visions - four beasts from the sea, a ram and a goat, seventy weeks, and a final revelation by the Tigris - tracing successive kingdoms and promising that the saints of the Most High will possess the kingdom forever.

Title: The Writing on the Wall
Events: At Belshazzar's feast a hand writes on the wall, and Daniel reads the writing: Belshazzar's kingdom has been weighed and is given to the Medes and Persians.

Title: Daniel in the Lions' Den
Events: Daniel keeps praying openly despite the royal decree, is thrown into the lions' den, and is delivered unharmed because he trusted in God.

Title: Esther in Persia
Events: Esther saves the Jewish people from Haman's plot; Purim instituted

Title: Return from Exile under Cyrus
KeyPersons: Cyrus the Great; Zerubbabel; Ezra; Nehemiah
Events: Cyrus allows exiles to return; Temple and Jerusalem walls rebuilt
ArchaeologicalFinds: Cyrus Cylinder (539 BC) records Cyrus's policy of restoring peoples and sanctuaries

Title: Rebuilding of the Temple
KeyPersons: Zerubbabel; Joshua the High Priest; Haggai; Zechariah
Events: The returned exiles rebuild the temple in Jerusalem despite opposition, finishing it in the sixth year of Darius and celebrating Passover.

Title: Zechariah's Fasting Question
Events: Men sent from Bethel ask the priests and prophets at Jerusalem whether they should keep mourning in the fifth month as they have for years, and Zechariah answers that God desires truth, mercy, and justice rather than fasting without obedience.

Title: Zechariah Breaks the Shepherd's Staffs
Events: Acting as shepherd of the flock doomed to slaughter, Zechariah takes two staffs, Favor and Union, and breaks them one after the other, then casts his wages of thirty pieces of silver to the potter, a sign that God's covenant favor and the brotherhood of Judah and Israel are broken.

Title: Ezra Confronts Intermarriage
Events: On arriving in Jerusalem, Ezra leads the people to confess and put away foreign marriages that threatened their covenant faithfulness.

Title: Ezra's Journey to Jerusalem
Events: Armed with Artaxerxes' decree and temple gifts, Ezra leads a caravan of exiles from Babylon to Jerusalem, fasting at the Ahava canal for a safe journey and delivering the silver and gold intact.

Title: Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall
Events: In fifty-two days Nehemiah leads the people to rebuild Jerusalem's broken wall despite mockery and threats from neighbouring governors.

Title: Ezra Reads the Law
Events: At the Water Gate, Ezra reads the Book of the Law aloud to all the people, who weep, worship, and celebrate the Feast of Booths.

Title: Book of Psalms Compiled
DateApprox: Individual psalms from David's time onward; final collection formed after the exile (date debated)
Events: One hundred and fifty psalms — Davidic psalms along with psalms of Asaph, the sons of Korah, and post-exilic psalms — are gathered into the five-book collection of the Psalter.

Title: Haggai's Call to Rebuild the Temple
Events: Haggai calls the returned exiles to stop paneling their own houses while God's house lies in ruins, and the people resume rebuilding the temple.

Title: Zechariah's Night Visions
DateApprox: 520-518 BC (second to fourth year of King Darius)
Events: Zechariah receives a series of night visions encouraging the returned exiles, promising that God will dwell in Jerusalem and cleanse his people.

Title: Second Temple and Post-Exilic Prophets
DateApprox: 520-516 BC Temple completed; prophets c. 520-430 BC
KeyPersons: Haggai; Zechariah; Malachi; Zerubbabel; Joshua the High Priest
Events: Haggai and Zechariah urge Temple rebuilding; Malachi closes OT prophecy

Title: Ecclesiastes Written
DateApprox: Traditionally Solomon c. 970-931 BC; many scholars date the book to the Persian or early Hellenistic period (date debated)
Events: The Teacher's reflection on the vanity of life under the sun, concluding with fearing God and keeping His commandments, is written as the book of Ecclesiastes.

Title: Malachi's Ministry
Events: Malachi, the last of the Old Testament prophets, rebukes corrupt worship and unfaithfulness and points forward to the messenger who will prepare the Lord's way.

Title: Dedication of Jerusalem's Wall
Events: With the wall rebuilt, two great choirs march in opposite directions around the wall to the temple, and the people celebrate with joy so loud it is heard far from Jerusalem.

Title: Nehemiah's Reforms
Events: Nehemiah confronts nobles who exploit the poor with loans, and on his second visit expels Tobiah from a temple storeroom, restores Levite support, and enforces the Sabbath.

Title: Between the Testaments
BibleBooks: (Historical background - no canonical Bible book covers this period in Protestant canon)
Events: Persian, Greek, and Roman rule; Maccabean Revolt (167-160 BC); Septuagint translated
ArchaeologicalFinds: Dead Sea Scrolls (c. 250 BC - AD 68, discovered 1947) preserve ancient OT manuscripts

Title: Birth of Jesus
KeyPersons: Jesus; Mary; Joseph; Herod the Great; Gabriel
Events: Angel announces Jesus's birth; born in Bethlehem; flight to Egypt

Title: Presentation of Jesus in the Temple
Events: In the temple at Jerusalem, Simeon takes the infant Jesus in his arms and blesses God, and the prophetess Anna gives thanks and speaks of him to all who waited for redemption.

Title: Visit of the Magi
KeyPersons: Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus; Joseph, Husband of Mary; Herod the Great
Events: Wise men from the east follow a star to Bethlehem, worship the child Jesus, and present gold, frankincense, and myrrh, then return home by another way after being warned in a dream.

Title: Massacre of the Innocents
Events: Herod, enraged at being outwitted by the wise men, orders the killing of all boys in Bethlehem and its vicinity who are two years old and under.

Title: Return from Egypt to Nazareth
KeyPersons: Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus; Joseph, Husband of Mary
Events: After Herod's death, Joseph is warned in a dream and brings Mary and Jesus back from Egypt, settling the family in Nazareth in Galilee.

Title: Boy Jesus in the Temple
KeyPersons: Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus; Joseph, Husband of Mary
Events: At twelve years old, Jesus stays behind in Jerusalem at Passover and is found in the temple, listening to the teachers and asking them questions, saying he must be about his Father's business.

Title: Baptism of Jesus
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: John baptizes Jesus in the Jordan, the Spirit descends on him, and a voice from heaven declares him the beloved Son.

Title: Temptation of Jesus in the Wilderness
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: After fasting forty days in the wilderness, Jesus resists Satan's three temptations by answering from Scripture.

Title: Calling of the Twelve Apostles
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
KeyPersons: Jesus; Simon Peter; Andrew; James, Son of Zebedee; Philip; Matthew; Thomas
Events: Jesus calls fishermen, a tax collector, and others to follow him and appoints twelve apostles to preach and heal.
ScriptureReference: Matthew 4:18-22; Matthew 10:1-4; Mark 1:16-20; Mark 3:13-19; Luke 5:1-11; Luke 6:12-16

Title: Water into Wine at Cana
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: At a wedding in Cana, Jesus turns water into wine, his first recorded miraculous sign.

Title: Jesus Calms the Storm
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Woken during a violent storm on the lake, Jesus rebukes the wind and waves and the sea becomes calm.

Title: Feeding of the Five Thousand
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Jesus multiplies five loaves and two fish to feed a crowd of about five thousand, with twelve baskets left over.

Title: Transfiguration of Jesus
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
KeyPersons: Jesus; Simon Peter; James, Son of Zebedee; John the Apostle
Events: On a high mountain Jesus is transfigured in glory before Peter, James, and John, and appears with Moses and Elijah.

Title: Healing of the Royal Official's Son
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: At Cana, Jesus tells a royal official whose son lies sick at Capernaum that his son lives, and the boy recovers at the very hour Jesus spoke.

Title: Healing at the Pool of Bethesda
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: At the pool of Bethesda in Jerusalem, Jesus heals a man who had been infirm for thirty-eight years, telling him to rise, take up his bed, and walk.

Title: Rejection at Nazareth
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: In his home town synagogue, Jesus reads from Isaiah and declares the Scripture fulfilled, but the people of Nazareth take offence and drive him out of the town.

Title: Demoniac in the Capernaum Synagogue
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: In the synagogue at Capernaum, Jesus rebukes an unclean spirit in a man, and the spirit cries out and comes out of him, amazing all who witness it.

Title: Healing of Peter's Mother-in-Law
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Jesus takes Simon Peter's mother-in-law, sick with a fever, by the hand, the fever leaves her, and she rises and serves them.

Title: Healing of a Leper
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: A leper kneels before Jesus asking to be made clean, Jesus touches him and says, I will, be thou clean, and the leprosy immediately departs.

Title: Healing of the Centurion's Servant
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: A Roman centurion asks Jesus to heal his servant from a distance, trusting his word alone, and Jesus marvels at his faith and heals the servant that same hour.

Title: Healing of the Paralytic Lowered Through the Roof
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Four men lower a paralysed man through the roof to Jesus, who first forgives his sins and then commands him to rise, take up his bed, and go home.

Title: Healing of the Man with a Withered Hand
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: On a sabbath in the synagogue, Jesus heals a man with a withered hand, answering those watching that it is lawful to do good on the sabbath.

Title: Healing of a Blind and Mute Demoniac
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Jesus heals a man who is blind and mute through demonic possession, so that he both speaks and sees, and the crowds wonder whether this is the Son of David.

Title: Healing of the Gerasene Demoniac
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Across the lake, Jesus meets a man possessed by a legion of demons, casts them into a herd of swine that rush into the sea, and leaves the man clothed and in his right mind.

Title: Healing of the Woman with a Flow of Blood
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: On the way to Jairus's house, a woman who had suffered twelve years touches the hem of Jesus' garment, is healed immediately, and is told her faith has made her whole.

Title: Raising of Jairus's Daughter
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Jesus goes to the house of Jairus, whose twelve-year-old daughter has died, takes her by the hand and says, Maid, arise, and she rises at once.

Title: Healing of Two Blind Men
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Two blind men follow Jesus crying for mercy as Son of David, Jesus touches their eyes, and their sight is restored according to their faith.

Title: Sending Out of the Twelve
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
KeyPersons: Jesus; Simon Peter; Andrew; James, Son of Zebedee; John the Apostle; Philip; Matthew; Thomas
Events: Jesus sends the twelve apostles out two by two to preach the kingdom, heal the sick, and cast out demons, giving them authority and instructions for the journey.

Title: Raising of the Widow's Son at Nain
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: At the gate of Nain, Jesus meets a funeral procession for a widow's only son, has compassion on her, touches the bier, and commands the young man to arise.

Title: Anointing by a Sinful Woman
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: At a Pharisee's table, a woman known as a sinner washes Jesus' feet with her tears, wipes them with her hair, and anoints them, and Jesus declares her many sins forgiven because she loved much.

Title: Beheading of John the Baptist
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
KeyPersons: John the Baptist; Herod Antipas; Herodias
Events: Herod Antipas, bound by a rash oath at a birthday feast and pressed by Herodias, orders John the Baptist beheaded in prison, and John's disciples bury his body.

Title: Walking on Water
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: In the night, after the feeding of the five thousand, Jesus walks on the sea to his disciples' boat, Peter briefly walks on the water toward him, and the wind ceases when Jesus enters the boat.

Title: Feeding of the Four Thousand
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: After three days with a crowd, Jesus multiplies seven loaves and a few small fishes to feed about four thousand, with seven baskets of fragments left over.

Title: Healing of the Syrophoenician Woman's Daughter
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: In the region of Tyre and Sidon, a Gentile woman persists in asking Jesus to heal her demon-possessed daughter, and Jesus commends her great faith and heals the girl from that hour.

Title: Healing of a Deaf Man in the Decapolis
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: In the Decapolis, people bring Jesus a man who is deaf and has an impediment in his speech, and Jesus opens his ears and loosens his tongue.

Title: Healing of a Blind Man at Bethsaida
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: At Bethsaida, Jesus takes a blind man by the hand, spits on his eyes and lays hands on him, and after a second touch the man sees clearly.

Title: Peter's Confession of Christ
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: At Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asks who the disciples say he is, and Peter answers, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God, and Jesus blesses his confession.

Title: Healing of a Boy with an Unclean Spirit
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: After the Transfiguration, Jesus heals a boy seized by a dumb spirit that the disciples could not cast out, rebuking the spirit and restoring the boy to his father.

Title: Sending Out of the Seventy-Two
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Jesus appoints seventy-two others and sends them ahead two by two into every town he will visit, to heal the sick and proclaim that the kingdom of God has come near.

Title: Woman Caught in Adultery
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Scribes and Pharisees bring a woman caught in adultery before Jesus, who writes on the ground and says, He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her, and her accusers leave one by one.

Title: Healing of a Man Born Blind
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Jesus makes clay, anoints the eyes of a man born blind, and sends him to wash in the pool of Siloam, and the man returns seeing, then testifies before the Pharisees.

Title: Healing of Ten Lepers
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: On the border between Galilee and Samaria, ten lepers cry for mercy, Jesus sends them to the priests, and all are cleansed as they go, though only one, a Samaritan, returns to give thanks.

Title: Healing of a Woman Bent Double
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: On a sabbath in the synagogue, Jesus lays hands on a woman bent double for eighteen years, she is immediately made straight, and glorifies God.

Title: Healing of a Man with Dropsy
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: On a sabbath at a Pharisee's house, Jesus heals a man with dropsy before the watching lawyers and Pharisees, asking whether it is lawful to heal on the sabbath.

Title: Raising of Lazarus
KeyPersons: Jesus; Lazarus; Martha; Mary of Bethany
Events: Four days after Lazarus dies, Jesus calls him out of the tomb alive, a sign that hardens the religious leaders' resolve to kill Jesus.

Title: Healing of Bartimaeus
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Near Jericho, blind Bartimaeus cries out, Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me, and Jesus restores his sight, and he follows Jesus on the way.

Title: Zacchaeus
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: At Jericho, the tax collector Zacchaeus climbs a sycamore tree to see Jesus, Jesus calls him down and stays at his house, and Zacchaeus repents, promising restitution and gifts to the poor.

Title: Anointing at Bethany
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: At Bethany, shortly before the Passover, Mary anoints Jesus' feet with costly ointment, and Jesus defends her, saying she has kept it for the day of his burial.

Title: Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Riding a donkey into Jerusalem, Jesus is acclaimed by crowds waving palm branches and crying Hosanna.

Title: Cleansing of the Temple
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Jesus drives out the money changers and sellers from the temple, overturning their tables, and declares that his Father's house shall be called a house of prayer.

Title: Cursing of the Fig Tree
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: On the way from Bethany to Jerusalem, Jesus finds a fig tree with leaves but no fruit, curses it, and by the next morning it has withered from the roots, prompting his teaching on faith and prayer.

Title: Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Judas Iscariot goes to the chief priests and agrees to betray Jesus to them for thirty pieces of silver, then seeks an opportunity to hand him over.

Title: Last Supper
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: At the Passover meal with his disciples, Jesus breaks bread and shares the cup as his body and blood and foretells his betrayal.

Title: Gethsemane
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
KeyPersons: Jesus; Simon Peter; James, Son of Zebedee; John the Apostle; Judas Iscariot
Events: In the garden of Gethsemane Jesus prays in anguish, submits to the Father's will, and is arrested after Judas betrays him with a kiss.

Title: Healing of Malchus's Ear
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: At Jesus' arrest in Gethsemane, Peter strikes the high priest's servant Malchus and cuts off his ear, and Jesus touches the ear and heals him.

Title: Peter Denies Jesus
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: While Jesus is on trial, Peter three times denies knowing him, as Jesus had foretold, and when the cock crows he remembers and weeps bitterly.

Title: Trial of Jesus before Pilate
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
KeyPersons: Jesus; Pontius Pilate; Caiaphas; Judas Iscariot
Events: After hearings before the Sanhedrin and Herod, Jesus is tried before the Roman governor Pilate, who sentences him to crucifixion.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Pilate Stone; Caiaphas Ossuary

Title: Death of Judas Iscariot
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Filled with remorse after Jesus is condemned, Judas returns the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests, casts them down in the temple, and goes and hangs himself.

Title: Crucifixion of Jesus
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
KeyPersons: Jesus; Simon Peter; Mary Magdalene; Pontius Pilate; Mary, mother of Jesus
Events: Jesus is crucified outside Jerusalem, dies, and darkness and an earthquake accompany his death.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Pilate Stone; Crucified Man of Giv'at ha-Mivtar (Yehohanan)

Title: Burial of Jesus
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Joseph of Arimathea lays Jesus' body in his own new tomb, which is sealed with a stone and guarded.

Title: Resurrection of Jesus
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
KeyPersons: Jesus; Mary Magdalene; Simon Peter; Thomas
Events: On the third day the tomb is found empty, and the risen Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene, the disciples, and Thomas.

Title: Jesus Appears on the Emmaus Road
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: On the first day of the week, the risen Jesus walks with two disciples on the road to Emmaus, opens the Scriptures to them, and is recognised in the breaking of bread.

Title: Jesus Appears by the Sea of Galilee and Restores Peter
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: By the Sea of Galilee, the risen Jesus directs a miraculous catch of fish, eats breakfast with the disciples, and three times asks Peter whether he loves him, restoring him and commissioning him to feed his sheep.

Title: Ascension of Jesus
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Forty days after his resurrection, Jesus blesses his disciples and ascends into heaven, commissioning them to wait for the Holy Spirit.

Title: Ministry, Death, and Resurrection of Jesus - Synoptic Gospels
KeyPersons: Jesus; John the Baptist; Peter; Mary Magdalene; Pontius Pilate
Events: Jesus teaches, heals, is crucified under Pilate, and rises; John gives theological account of the Word made flesh
ArchaeologicalFinds: Pilate Stone (discovered Caesarea, 1961) names Pontius Pilate; Caiaphas Ossuary

Title: Pentecost and Birth of the Church
Events: Holy Spirit descends at Pentecost; church spreads; Stephen martyred

Title: Choosing of Matthias
Events: After the Ascension, the disciples pray and cast lots to choose Matthias to take Judas's place among the twelve apostles.

Title: Healing of the Lame Man at the Beautiful Gate
Events: At the temple's Beautiful Gate, Peter and John heal a man lame from birth, who rises, walks, and leaps, praising God, drawing a crowd in Solomon's porch.

Title: Peter and John Before the Sanhedrin
Events: Arrested for preaching the resurrection, Peter and John are brought before the Sanhedrin, boldly declare healing in Jesus' name, and are threatened and released.

Title: Ananias and Sapphira
KeyPersons: Simon Peter; Ananias, Husband of Sapphira; Sapphira
Events: Ananias and his wife Sapphira sell land but secretly keep back part of the price while presenting it as the whole, and each falls dead after Peter exposes the lie to the Holy Spirit.

Title: Apostles Imprisoned and Freed by an Angel
KeyPersons: Simon Peter; John the Apostle; Gamaliel, the Pharisee
Events: The high priest imprisons the apostles, but an angel frees them by night and they return to preaching in the temple, and Gamaliel counsels the council to leave them alone.

Title: Choosing of the Seven
Events: To settle a complaint that widows were neglected in the daily distribution, the apostles have the church choose seven men full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, including Stephen and Philip, to serve the tables.

Title: Peter Heals Aeneas
Events: At Lydda, Peter finds Aeneas, bedridden with palsy for eight years, and says, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole, and Aeneas rises at once.

Title: Peter Raises Tabitha
Events: At Joppa, the disciple Tabitha, known for her good works, dies, and Peter prays, says, Tabitha, arise, and presents her alive to the widows and saints.

Title: Martyrdom of Stephen
Events: Stephen, the first Christian martyr, is stoned after testifying before the Sanhedrin, while Saul approves of his death.

Title: Philip in Samaria and Simon the Sorcerer
Events: Philip preaches Christ in Samaria, many believe and are baptised, and Simon the sorcerer, who had amazed the city, seeks to buy the power of giving the Holy Spirit and is rebuked by Peter.

Title: Philip and the Ethiopian Eunuch
Events: Directed by an angel to the desert road to Gaza, Philip joins an Ethiopian official reading Isaiah, explains that the passage speaks of Jesus, and baptises him, after which Philip is caught away.

Title: Saul's Escape from Damascus
Events: After Saul begins preaching Christ in Damascus, the Jews plot to kill him and watch the city gates, so the disciples lower him down through the wall in a basket by night.

Title: Church at Antioch
Events: Believers scattered by the persecution after Stephen preach to Gentiles at Antioch, Barnabas encourages the growing church, Saul is brought to teach there, and the disciples are first called Christians.

Title: Peter Escapes from Prison
KeyPersons: Simon Peter; James, Son of Zebedee; Herod Agrippa I
Events: Herod Agrippa kills James the brother of John with the sword and imprisons Peter, intending to bring him out after Passover, but an angel frees Peter by night and he goes to the house where believers are praying.

Title: Death of Herod Agrippa I
Events: At Caesarea, Herod Agrippa accepts the people's cry that his voice is a god's, and because he does not give God glory, he is struck down by an angel and eaten by worms.

Title: James Writes His Letter
Events: James, the brother of Jesus and leader of the Jerusalem church, writes to Jewish Christians scattered abroad, urging patient endurance and a faith that shows itself in works.

Title: Elymas Struck Blind
Events: At Paphos, the sorcerer Elymas tries to turn the proconsul Sergius Paulus from the faith, and Paul declares him blind for a season, so that Elymas gropes for someone to lead him and the proconsul believes.

Title: Healing of a Lame Man at Lystra
Events: At Lystra, Paul heals a man crippled from birth, and the crowds, thinking the gods have come down, try to sacrifice to Barnabas and Paul, who restrain them and preach the living God.

Title: Paul Stoned at Lystra
Events: Jews from Antioch and Iconium persuade the crowds at Lystra to stone Paul and drag him out of the city, supposing him dead, but he rises and the next day departs with Barnabas to Derbe.

Title: Paul Writes Galatians
Events: Paul writes to the churches of Galatia, insisting that Gentile believers are justified by faith in Christ, not by keeping the law of Moses.

Title: Paul Confronts Peter at Antioch
Events: When Cephas (Peter) came to Antioch, he first ate with Gentile believers and then withdrew when men from James arrived. Paul opposed him publicly, saying Peter was not acting in line with the truth of the gospel, since Gentile believers were not required to live like Jews.

Title: Paul's Vision of the Macedonian Man
Events: At Troas by night, Paul sees a vision of a man of Macedonia pleading, Come over into Macedonia, and help us, and the mission party concludes that God has called them to preach there.

Title: Paul and Silas Imprisoned at Philippi
Events: At Philippi, Paul and Silas are beaten and imprisoned after casting a spirit out of a slave girl, an earthquake opens the prison at midnight prayer, and the jailer and his household believe and are baptised.

Title: Riot at Thessalonica
Events: At Thessalonica, jealous Jews stir up a mob against Paul and Silas, drag Jason before the city rulers for harbouring men who proclaim another king, Jesus, and Paul and Silas are sent away by night to Berea.

Title: Paul in Athens
Events: At Athens, Paul is stirred by the city's idols, reasons in the synagogue and marketplace, and speaks at the Areopagus about the unknown God, with some believing, including Dionysius and Damaris.

Title: Paul's Night Vision at Corinth
Events: At Corinth, the Lord speaks to Paul in a night vision, telling him not to be afraid but to speak, for no one will harm him and many people in the city belong to God.

Title: Paul Before Gallio
Events: Jews bring Paul before Gallio, proconsul of Achaia, accusing him of persuading men to worship contrary to the law, but Gallio dismisses the case as a matter of words and names and drives them from the judgment seat.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Gallio Inscription

Title: Paul Writes 1 Thessalonians
Events: Paul writes from Corinth to the young church at Thessalonica, encouraging them in persecution and answering their questions about the return of Christ.

Title: Paul Writes 2 Thessalonians
Events: Paul writes a second letter to Thessalonica, correcting confusion about the day of the Lord and urging steady, orderly work while they wait.

Title: Sons of Sceva
Events: At Ephesus, seven sons of Sceva try to cast out an evil spirit by invoking the Jesus whom Paul preaches, but the possessed man overpowers them and they flee naked and wounded, so that the name of Jesus is magnified.

Title: Riot at Ephesus
Events: Demetrius the silversmith, fearing loss of trade from shrines of Artemis, stirs the craftsmen into a riot that fills the theatre at Ephesus for two hours, until the town clerk disperses the assembly.

Title: Paul Raises Eutychus at Troas
Events: At Troas, as Paul preaches late into the night, the young man Eutychus falls asleep in a window, falls three stories, and is taken up dead, but Paul embraces him and he is brought alive.

Title: Paul Writes 1 Corinthians
Events: Paul writes from Ephesus to the divided and disordered church at Corinth, addressing factions, immorality, worship, and the resurrection.

Title: Paul Writes 2 Corinthians
Events: Paul writes again to Corinth from Macedonia, defending his apostleship, describing his sufferings, and urging generous giving and reconciliation.

Title: Paul Writes Romans
Events: Paul writes from Corinth to the church at Rome, setting out the gospel of justification by faith ahead of his planned visit on the way to Spain.

Title: Paul Arrested in Jerusalem
Events: At Jerusalem, Jews from Asia seize Paul in the temple, accusing him of defiling it, a mob tries to kill him, and the Roman commander rescues him and takes him into the barracks.

Title: Paul Before the Sanhedrin and the Plot Against Him
KeyPersons: Paul; Ananias, the High Priest; Claudius Lysias
Events: Before the Sanhedrin, Paul's declaration divides Pharisees and Sadducees, a plot of more than forty men to kill him is revealed by his nephew, and the commander sends Paul by night under guard to Caesarea.

Title: Paul Before Felix
Events: At Caesarea, Tertullus accuses Paul before Governor Felix, Paul defends himself, Felix keeps him in custody for two years, hearing him often about faith in Christ, until Festus succeeds him.

Title: Paul Before Festus and Agrippa
KeyPersons: Paul; Festus; Herod Agrippa II; Bernice
Events: Before Festus at Caesarea, Paul appeals to Caesar rather than face trial at Jerusalem, and then defends himself before King Agrippa and Bernice, who conclude he has done nothing worthy of death or bonds.

Title: Healing of Publius's Father on Malta
